limitations: Three samples per arm establish neither tail percentiles nor a latency guarantee.
Sequential arms include provider scheduling and network variation; small differences cannot establish causality.
Fresh wallets do not guarantee cold Workers. Worker cold starts were not controlled.
Invocation wall time can include background work and is not browser response time.
Nested spans overlap. Protocol spans include transport; zero Worker clock spans do not prove zero CPU.
Existing bound-root counters cover six D1 calls, not all database work in registration.
The removed shared-record reads are three SQL statements in existing batches; they do not remove three HTTP calls.
Requested APAC placement does not prove physical colocation.

decision.reason: Ceremony-only reads remove unrelated shared capability access and reduce CPU in all three changed Gateway paths. This is retained as a bounded data-access and CPU reduction, without claiming a full registration speedup.
decision.nextExperiment: Compare native Durable Object RPC against the existing HTTP dispatch for real Router claim and consume commands. Preserve ownership generation, claim leases, relocation fences and exact retries. Reuse existing staging resources, remove an unsuccessful candidate, and do not repeat the already-rejected global handle-cache experiment.
